catalog.name: Fire & Vegetation Change Monitoring
catalog.description: Fire detection and vegetation change products from MODIS and VIIRS missions providing critical information for wildfire monitoring, land use change detection, and ecosystem management.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: Fire products from NASA MODIS and VIIRS missions, processed by NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System). Land cover data from NASA Land Processes Distributed Active Archive Center (LP DAAC). Contact: earthdata-support@nasa.gov

info.name: License
info.content: NASA data is generally available for public use. Real-time fire data is provided for emergency response and resource management applications.

info.name: Early Warning Applications
info.content: Fire detection products provide near real-time alerts for wildfire response, enabling rapid deployment of firefighting resources and early evacuation warnings for populated areas.

info.name: Ecosystem Management
info.content: Long-term fire and vegetation datasets support prescribed fire planning, post-fire recovery monitoring, and ecosystem restoration efforts.

members.name: Active Fire Detection
members.description: Near real-time fire detection products using thermal anomaly detection algorithms to identify actively burning fires and thermal hotspots.

members.name: MODIS Active Fire (Terra, Daily)
members.description: Daily active fire detections from MODIS Terra satellite using thermal infrared bands to identify fires and thermal anomalies with high confidence levels.

info.name: Background
info.content: MODIS active fire products use middle infrared (3.9 μm) and thermal infrared (11-12 μm) bands to detect thermal anomalies characteristic of fires. The algorithm identifies pixels significantly warmer than their surroundings.

info.name: Detection Method
info.content: Uses contextual fire detection algorithm comparing target pixel brightness temperature to background pixels, with multiple tests to reject false alarms from hot surfaces, sun glint, and other sources

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 1 km nominal resolution with sub-pixel fire detection capability for fires as small as 0.1% of pixel area under optimal conditions

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: February 2000 to present, daily global coverage from Terra satellite morning overpass (~10:30 AM local time)

info.name: Confidence Levels
info.content: Fire pixels classified as high confidence (>80%), nominal confidence (30-80%), or low confidence (<30%) based on detection algorithm performance

info.name: Detection Limitations
info.content: May miss small fires, fires under heavy smoke or cloud cover, and fires with low thermal contrast. Optimal detection during early morning overpass times

info.name: Applications
info.content: Wildfire monitoring, fire weather analysis, emissions inventory, fire danger assessment, rapid response fire mapping, prescribed fire monitoring

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)

members.name: MODIS Active Fire (Aqua, Daily)
members.description: Daily active fire detections from MODIS Aqua satellite providing complementary afternoon fire detection to enhance overall fire monitoring capability.

info.name: Background
info.content: MODIS Aqua provides complementary fire detection to Terra MODIS, with afternoon overpass enabling detection of fires that develop during daytime heating or may be missed by morning observations.

info.name: Overpass Time
info.content: Aqua satellite has afternoon overpass (~1:30 PM local time) complementing Terra's morning overpass for enhanced daily fire detection coverage

info.name: Complementary Value
info.content: Combined Terra and Aqua observations provide improved fire detection with two daily observation opportunities and better temporal sampling of fire activity

info.name: Diurnal Fire Patterns
info.content: Afternoon overpass captures peak fire activity periods when many fires reach maximum intensity due to daytime heating and lower humidity

info.name: Applications
info.content: Enhanced fire detection when combined with Terra, fire behavior analysis, diurnal fire pattern studies, improved fire event mapping

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, NASA FIRMS

members.name: VIIRS Active Fire (Day/Night, Daily)
members.description: Daily active fire detections from VIIRS instrument with higher spatial resolution and day/night fire detection capability for comprehensive fire monitoring.

info.name: Background
info.content: VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) provides enhanced fire detection with higher spatial resolution than MODIS and capability to detect fires during both day and night overpasses.

info.name: Enhanced Resolution
info.content: 375m spatial resolution providing significantly higher detail than MODIS 1km fire products, enabling detection of smaller fires and more precise fire location

info.name: Day/Night Detection
info.content: Capable of fire detection during both daytime and nighttime overpasses, providing up to 4 daily observation opportunities for fire monitoring

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: January 2012 to present from Suomi NPP satellite, with continuing operations planned

info.name: Detection Algorithm
info.content: Uses similar contextual fire detection approach as MODIS but optimized for VIIRS spectral bands and higher spatial resolution

info.name: Unique Capabilities
info.content: Superior small fire detection, nighttime fire monitoring, higher spatial precision for fire location, improved detection in heterogeneous landscapes

info.name: Applications
info.content: High-resolution fire mapping, small fire detection, nighttime fire monitoring, precision fire location for response teams, detailed fire behavior analysis

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA/NOAA VIIRS mission team, NASA FIRMS

members.name: Burn Area and Fire Impact
members.description: Post-fire burn area mapping and fire impact assessment products for quantifying fire effects on ecosystems and landscapes.

members.name: MODIS Burned Area (Monthly)
members.description: Monthly global burned area product mapping areas affected by fire using multitemporal analysis of MODIS surface reflectance data.

info.name: Background
info.content: The MODIS Burned Area product uses bidirectional reflectance characteristics and temporal changes in surface reflectance to identify areas affected by fire during each month.

info.name: Mapping Approach
info.content: Uses combination of surface reflectance changes, vegetation indices, and active fire information to map burn areas with temporal precision to approximate day of burning

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 500m spatial resolution providing detailed burn area mapping for fire impact assessment

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: November 2000 to present, monthly global burned area products

info.name: Product Features
info.content: Includes burn date, burn area extent, and quality assessment information for each detected burn area

info.name: Validation
info.content: Extensively validated against Landsat-derived burn areas and field observations, with regional accuracy assessments available

info.name: Applications
info.content: Fire impact assessment, carbon emissions estimation, post-fire recovery monitoring, fire regime analysis, land management planning

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, University of Maryland fire team, NASA GSFC

members.name: Fire Radiative Power (Daily)
members.description: Daily fire radiative power measurements quantifying energy release rates from active fires for fire intensity assessment and emissions estimation.

info.name: Background
info.content: Fire Radiative Power (FRP) measures the rate of energy release from fires, providing quantitative information about fire intensity and enabling estimation of fuel consumption and emissions.

info.name: Measurement Units
info.content: Measured in Megawatts (MW), representing the rate of radiant energy release from fires

info.name: Scientific Basis
info.content: FRP is directly related to fuel consumption rates and can be used to estimate smoke emissions, trace gas release, and fire behavior characteristics

info.name: Applications
info.content: Fire behavior analysis, emissions inventory development, air quality forecasting, fire danger assessment, fire management planning

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, King's College London fire research group

members.name: Vegetation and Land Cover Change
members.description: Long-term vegetation monitoring and land cover change products for tracking ecosystem changes, deforestation, and landscape modifications.

members.name: MODIS Land Cover Type (Annual)
members.description: Annual global land cover classification showing vegetation types, land use patterns, and ecosystem distributions with multiple classification schemes.

info.name: Background
info.content: MODIS Land Cover Type provides annual global land cover classifications using supervised machine learning algorithms applied to MODIS surface reflectance and land surface temperature data.

info.name: Classification Schemes
info.content: Multiple classification systems including IGBP (International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme), University of Maryland scheme, and Plant Functional Type classifications

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 500m spatial resolution enabling detailed land cover mapping and change detection

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: 2001 to present, annual global land cover products enabling 20+ years of land cover change analysis

info.name: Land Cover Classes
info.content: 17 IGBP classes including forests, grasslands, croplands, urban areas, wetlands, and other natural and human-modified landscapes

info.name: Change Detection
info.content: Time series analysis enables detection of deforestation, afforestation, agricultural expansion, urban growth, and other land cover transitions

info.name: Applications
info.content: Ecosystem monitoring, deforestation tracking, carbon cycle studies, biodiversity assessment, climate modeling, land use planning

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, Boston University land cover team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center

members.name: Enhanced Vegetation Index (16-Day)
members.description: 16-day composite Enhanced Vegetation Index showing vegetation productivity and phenology patterns with improved sensitivity in high biomass areas.

info.name: Background
info.content: Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) provides improved vegetation monitoring compared to NDVI, with reduced atmospheric and canopy background effects and enhanced sensitivity in high biomass regions.

info.name: Index Formula
info.content: EVI = 2.5 * ((NIR - Red) / (NIR + 6*Red - 7.5*Blue + 1)), incorporating blue band correction for atmospheric effects

info.name: Composite Period
info.content: 16-day composites using maximum value approach to reduce cloud contamination and provide consistent vegetation monitoring

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 250m spatial resolution enabling detailed vegetation analysis and landscape-scale monitoring

info.name: Phenology Applications
info.content: Excellent for tracking vegetation phenology, growing season timing, productivity changes, and ecosystem response to environmental conditions

info.name: Fire Recovery Monitoring
info.content: Particularly valuable for monitoring post-fire vegetation recovery and ecosystem restoration following disturbances

info.name: Applications
info.content: Vegetation productivity monitoring, phenology studies, post-fire recovery assessment, ecosystem health evaluation, agricultural monitoring

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, University of Arizona vegetation index team

members.name: Leaf Area Index (8-Day)
members.description: 8-day Leaf Area Index representing vegetation density and canopy structure for ecosystem productivity and carbon cycle studies.

info.name: Background
info.content: Leaf Area Index (LAI) represents the amount of leaf area in an ecosystem and is fundamental for understanding ecosystem productivity, carbon cycling, and vegetation-atmosphere interactions.

info.name: Definition
info.content: LAI is defined as the one-sided leaf area per unit ground surface area (m²/m²), providing quantitative measure of vegetation density

info.name: Temporal Resolution
info.content: 8-day composites providing frequent monitoring of vegetation dynamics and seasonal changes

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 500m resolution suitable for ecosystem-scale vegetation monitoring and modeling applications

info.name: Carbon Cycle Relevance
info.content: LAI is directly related to photosynthetic capacity and primary productivity, making it essential for carbon cycle modeling

info.name: Fire Impact Assessment
info.content: Changes in LAI following fires provide quantitative assessment of fire impacts on vegetation density and ecosystem structure

info.name: Applications
info.content: Ecosystem productivity modeling, carbon cycle studies, climate modeling, post-disturbance recovery monitoring, forest management

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MODIS mission team, NASA GSFC biophysical products team
